claims.text: Microsoft's Azure business crossed $100 billion in trailing/fiscal-year revenue (FY2026).
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion in Q2 2026, up from $106 billion a year earlier.
AWS's AI business and its chips business (Trainium and Graviton) each exceeded a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate, growing triple-digit percentages year-over-year.
Gartner forecast that worldwide public cloud spending will exceed $1 trillion in 2027.
According to Gartner, by 2028 cloud-native platforms will be the foundation for more than 95% of new digital initiatives, up from less than 50% in 2023.
AWS posted $42.2 billion revenue in Q2 2026, up 37% year-over-year, accelerating from 28% growth the prior quarter, its fastest growth since 2021.
Microsoft Azure revenue grew 43% year-over-year in fiscal Q4 2026 (ended June 30, 2026), up from 40% the prior quarter; Nadella said Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time.
Google Cloud revenue rose 82% year-over-year to $24.8 billion in Q2 2026.
Alphabet raised its full-year 2026 capex guidance to $195–205 billion, up from $180–190 billion that had already been raised twice this year.

Oracle reported FY2026 cloud revenue of $34.0 billion, up 39% year-over-year, with remaining performance obligations of $638 billion, up 363%, including prepaid and customer-supplied GPU deals totaling $75 billion.
Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers found 64% run on AWS, 55% on Google Cloud, and 45% on Azure.
Gartner forecasts total worldwide AI spending will reach $2.59 trillion in 2026, a 47% increase year-over-year.
IDC predicts that by 2027 half of enterprises will be using AI agents.
Gartner predicts that by 2028 over 50% of enterprises will use AI security platforms, with spending on securing AI reaching roughly $4.8 billion in 2027.
Gartner says by 2026, 80% of large software engineering organizations will establish platform engineering teams.

CNCF's Q1 2026 Technology Radar report with SlashData found 28% of surveyed organizations have a dedicated platform engineering team and 35% run a hybrid platform combining developer platforms with AI tooling.
Chris Aniszczyk, CTO of CNCF, made the quoted statement about cloud native platforms and AI workloads.
Gartner predicts agentic AI deployment in IT operations grows from under 5% in 2025 to 70% by 2029, while human-in-the-loop requirements fall from 95% in 2025 to 40% by 2028.

Pulumi's 2026 survey: 82% agree AI agents will change how they write infrastructure within 12 months; 63% say they trust agents for production changes; expectation of agents generating half or more of code rises from 45% to 52% within six months.
Pulumi Neo proposes infrastructure changes, runs previews, and executes approved updates with policy guardrails.
According to Mordor Intelligence, the global Kubernetes market is USD 3.13 billion in 2026, projected to reach USD 8.41 billion by 2031, a 21.85% CAGR.

CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report puts cloud-native adoption among ML/AI developers at 41%, and 30% of backend developers using Kubernetes directly, down from a 36% peak in Q3 2023, which the report attributes to maturity.
The July 2026 revision of the Model Context Protocol is described by its maintainers as the largest revision to date.
AWS shipped a generally available MCP server for its Agent Toolkit, and Mirantis's Lens launched a built-in MCP server.
Gartner says by 2028, 75% of enterprise software engineers will use AI code assistants, and 63% of organizations are piloting, deploying or beginning to use them.
Cloud infrastructure is entering its most transformative era since the rise of Kubernetes.
